⚙️ Engineered Features

8 new features derived from base columns to enable richer modelling and segmentation.

FeatureTypeFormula / LogicPurpose
Age_GroupOrdinal Cat.pd.cut(Age, [0,25,35,45,55,100])Life-stage segmentation
Income_TierOrdinal Cat.Tertile split (33rd / 67th pct)Affordability segment
Engagement_ScoreFloat [0–1]0.35×Time + 0.30×Pages + 0.35×PurchaseFreq (normalised)Single engagement KPI
Revenue_Per_VisitFloatTotal_Spending / (Time_on_Site_hrs)Spend efficiency
Recency_ScoreIntmax(Last_Login) − Last_LoginRFM recency component
CLV_ProxyIntAOV × Purchase_FrequencyCustomer lifetime value proxy
Interest_Category_MatchBinaryMap Interest→expected Category, comparePreference alignment flag
Power_UserBinaryEngagement_Score ≥ Q75 AND Newsletter=TrueHigh-value user flag

1. Demographics Overview

Demographics Overview

Age distribution skews towards mid-life (mean 41). Gender and Location are well-balanced. The 26–55 age range accounts for ~60% of users.

2. Spending & Income Analysis

Spending & Income Analysis

Income is broadly uniform. Total Spending is right-skewed with most users below $3K. High-income tier users spend only marginally more on average.

3. User Engagement Metrics

User Engagement Metrics

Engagement Score follows a roughly normal distribution centred at 0.5. Time on Site and Pages Viewed are positively correlated. Middle age groups show peak engagement.

4. Interests & Product Preferences

Interests & Product Preferences

Interests and preferred categories are evenly distributed across the 5 options each — no single dominant group. Apparel leads product preference by a slim margin.

5. Feature Correlation Heatmap

Feature Correlation Heatmap

CLV Proxy and Purchase Frequency are highly correlated. Engagement Score correlates moderately with Pages Viewed and Time on Site. Income shows near-zero correlation with most behavioural metrics.

6. Revenue & CLV Insights

Revenue & CLV Insights

CLV Proxy scales linearly with Purchase Frequency. Location has minimal influence on CLV. Newsletter subscribers show a clear engagement advantage.

7. User Segmentation & Power Users

User Segmentation & Power Users

Segment sizes are balanced across Income Tier × Age Group combinations. Power Users (12.8%) are the top-engagement, newsletter-subscribed cohort worth targeting for retention campaigns.
